arm_pairing: Arms A and B are evaluated on ONE shared agent session per task, recorded as arm 'AB'. Arm B adds only a verification GATE and gives the agent no feedback, so by construction the agent's behaviour in A and B is identical; running two sessions would double the cost and add independent sampling noise to a comparison that is meant to be paired. Each AB record therefore carries both decision rules — arm_A_decision (accept iff the project's own tests pass) and arm_B_decision (accept iff the independent oracle verifies) — applied to the same measured output, plus ground_truth_correct from the oracle. Arm C is a separate session because it feeds counterexamples back to the agent.
